analysis: This PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the 'Last updated' date (line 3) and adds one failure-mode table row, head line 2316. That row documents a cold load refused with a 503 or insufficient-memory error when an idle resident model holds an unexpired Autopilot placement hold. It cites ProviderLoop.evictableModelSlots, autopilotHoldsModel and autopilotHeldWeightBytes, and links model-autopilot.md. No code, configuration, cryptographic, attestation, authorization or wire-protocol behavior changes. The two supplied units are base-text excerpts of this file, and the surrounding text is unchanged. I examined them against the relevant threat model, T-041 (prefix-cache and SSD at-rest posture) and the TB-002/TB-003/TB-007/TB-011 boundaries. The changed row is descriptive. It does not weaken the cache TTL, HMAC lookup tags, salt scoping, KEK custody, coordinator-authored cache scope or serving authorization. The documented behavior, that held slots are excluded from eviction and get no reclaim credit, is an availability and resource-management note. Operationally, a placement hold could make a cold load fail while an idle model stays resident, which touches availability. But that behavior lives in code not supplied here (Autopilot/ProviderLoop+AutopilotPlacement.swift), and the documentation row only describes it. I did not verify that the described behavior matches the implementation, or how placement holds are granted and expire. That is an integration question outside this docs-only change. No new attack surface or threat-model invalidation was identified.
